scope: Controlled asynchronous buffer-recovery lifecycle checks; no official game equivalence or physical latency measurement
reproduced: While an old media play observation remains pending, pause/restart leaves streamRecoveryPending set and blocks a later recovery.
An old recovery completion calls pause() on the actual replacement HTML media while its new start is pending; the before browser recording changes paused false -> true and the real clock stops.
An old open-ended inputClockPauses interval can classify resumed inputs as buffered, and its late finally closes it at the wrong time.
changes: Synchronously release and abort recovery ownership on reset/pause/stop.
Close the owned input interval on cancellation and do not extend it when an old callback returns.
Restrict progress, final cleanup and scheduling to the owning controller/session; stale completion does not pause shared audio.
Keep current recovery errors visible through the existing manual-pause/error path; normal contact and timing regressions remain enabled.

commands.command: git diff --check; node --check js/app.js; node --check tests/stream-recovery-browser.cjs

browserMethod: Force the existing HTML media fallback by a controlled Web Audio prepare failure. Play the real local Leave All Behind EZ audio. Simulate an underflow through readiness getters and delay only unmuted play-promise observations; the native play/pause, stream wait, actual Engine restart/resume and music clock still run. Muted gesture-prime calls are not delayed. This is a controlled I/O ordering regression, not an organic network/Safari reproduction.
browserOutcomes: Before: native media playing before the overlap is paused by the old callback, and currentTime does not advance.
After: replacement remains unpaused and its native media clock advances.
After manual pause/resume, input is not classified in the old buffering interval; a new recovery keeps its own controller, progress handler and visible status when the old callback settles.
limitations: No official judgment-window, timing, audiovisual-sync or physical device/Safari equivalence conclusion.
Controlled promises model late callbacks; this does not measure their frequency on a real network.
Other asynchronous gesture-prime, audio activation and optional transport paths are outside this regression.
Official baseline, complete resources, visuals, animations, Tips, chapters/replay and real-user save compatibility remain unaccepted as recorded in docs/fidelity-acceptance.json.
